analysis.title: A fragile AI rebound
key_insights: Equities rose despite a hot October CPI print (third consecutive beat) that drove a sharp rates selloff. The rally was led by AI catalysts: CoreWeave's results, Anthropic's oversubscribed IPO and OpenAI revenues. MSCI World is up about 3% this week and has erased last week's drawdown.

Sentiment turned negative this morning on reports that Nvidia's board is considering replacing J. Huang. Nvidia fell as much as 10% in after-hours trading. AI and tech stocks in Asia are weighed down, and Alibaba fell as much as 7% on fears of tighter US scrutiny. AMD, Broadcom and Alphabet gained after hours on bets they could win business from Nvidia.

A 25bp Fed hike is fully priced for next month, with a non-trivial chance of a half-point move. Natixis calls a jumbo hike a live possibility but keeps a 25bp hike as its base case, consistent with the Fed's stated preference for a gradual and cautious approach. The outcome depends on financial conditions and data strength before the December 9 meeting.

Treasuries sold off after the hotter-than-expected CPI. The US 2Y rose 17 bps and the 10Y rose 11.4 bps to 5%. Bunds and Gilts followed (German 10Y 3.32%, UK 10Y 5.22%). Cash Treasuries were closed Wednesday for Veterans Day, but futures kept falling. Long-end Treasuries saw modest safe-haven demand this morning on the Nvidia risk-off tone.

The dollar hit its highest since May 2025, with DXY up 1.2% to 102.90 on the CPI-driven December hike expectations. EUR/USD fell 1.0% to 1.1093 and GBP/USD fell 1.1% to 1.3275. USD/JPY broke above 159.86, a level last seen in early September.

Emerging-market currencies weakened broadly. IDR is near record lows and BRL is at a 15-month low on dovish BCB minutes. IDR is under additional pressure as Indonesia's VP resigns, on policy risk premium and recent MSCI warnings about removing Indonesia from the index, with passive outflows continuing. Natixis stays cautious on IDR and Indonesia. CNH was relatively stable.
Gold fell 2.7% on the stronger dollar and rising real yields.

Equity moves: Nikkei +4.2%, Euro Stoxx 50 +1.6%, S&P 500 +1.1%. Nasdaq was lifted by Nvidia (+4% on the session), CoreWeave (+24%) and Anthropic IPO optimism. Hang Seng lagged at -0.5% on EM currency pressure from hawkish Fed repricing. MSCI EM gained 1.6% on Asian chipmakers (TSMC, SK Hynix, Samsung).

Credit: Main tightened 1.5 bps and X-Over 8 bps. In hybrids, real estate (Aroundtown, CPI) and autos (mainly Volkswagen) outperformed. CoreWeave's euro 8.5% 2032 bond gained 4.7 price points and its USD bonds gained 1 to 2 points. Five-year CDS on Oracle tightened 2.5 bps and on Broadcom 1 bp.

CoreWeave Q3-26 gave short-term relief without ending capital-structure and regulatory overhangs. Revenue was $3.7bn (+168% YoY) vs $3.6bn consensus, with a $132.5bn backlog. EPS was -$1.27 vs -$1.46 expected. FY-26 revenue guidance was raised to $13.0-$13.3bn from $12-$13bn. Funding remains the debate: FY-26 capex is seen at $37-$39bn and Q4-26 interest expense at $1.05-$1.15bn.

CoreWeave's funding plan: weighted average cost of debt fell 250 bps sequentially to 7.9% and a DDTL facility is coming. Management ruled out unsecured debt at current yields and plans to rely on client prepayments ($9bn expected next quarter). It capped 2027 parent-level capital raises at $5bn.

Siemens raised its 2027 revenue growth outlook to +11% from +9%, with Digital Industries growth guided above the +8% consensus (range 8-12%). The raise rests on industrial AI and data-center demand, implying 58% order backlog growth in Q4 2026 to nearly EUR35bn vs EUR28bn expected.

UK Q3 preliminary GDP was +0.7% QoQ, the fastest in two and a half years, and September monthly growth was +0.2% MoM vs flat consensus. UK front-end yields stay sticky and markets expect the Bank of England to keep hiking.

South Korea's exports rose 112% YoY in the first 10 days, driven by chips, and unemployment fell to 2.5%. Consumption is subdued by higher rates and worse sentiment. Kospi is down despite yesterday's rally, giving the BOK room to stay on hold this month.

European office development remains constrained, per Cushman & Wakefield. Prime rents are up 23% since 2022, and viability is forecast to recover in CBDs region-wide by late 2029, with Paris turning positive in 2027 and London City possibly after 2030.

Other credit and sector news: S&P affirmed Altarea at BBB-/Stable, RWE reaffirmed 2026 EBITDA guidance at the upper end of EUR5.75-6.35bn, EDF wants changes to river-temperature rules after curtailing 7 reactors in summer 2026, the UK is reportedly cutting its 2030 ZEV target to 60% from 80%, and French authorities are expected to block CSG's acquisition of Dixi Microtechniques.

Nvidia leadership turmoil, with reports its board is considering replacing J. Huang, is weighing on AI and tech stocks.
CoreWeave's capital structure and regulatory overhangs persist, with heavy FY-26 capex of $37-$39bn and Q4-26 interest expense of $1.05-$1.15bn.
EM currency pressure from the strong dollar and Fed repricing. IDR has idiosyncratic policy and index-removal risk.
China's self-sufficiency trade faces a valuation reset.

Passive outflows from Indonesia continue after MSCI warnings about removing it from the index.

geopolitical: Indonesia's VP resigned, adding political risk to IDR on top of recent MSCI warnings about removing Indonesia from its index.
Fears of tighter US scrutiny weighed on Alibaba.
French authorities are expected to block Czech defense group CSG from acquiring Dixi Microtechniques, a maker of fuzes supplying KNDS and Rheinmetall, over supply-chain control concerns.

tension_points.bull_case: AI catalysts (CoreWeave's beat and raise, Anthropic's oversubscribed IPO, OpenAI revenues) pushed MSCI World up about 3% on the week despite the hot CPI print. Siemens' data-center-driven backlog outlook adds support.
